question: How often do pairs of original MODERN insect sampling localities contact the same connected potential 0BP vs 21ka host climate patch? Geometry only; no historical insect occurrences or genetic differentiation.

methods.terrain: ICE6G_C reconstruction passable source icefree land if >=5/9 10arcminute subcells, separate 0BP and 21ka.
methods.host_resource: OR of all recorded host plant potential suitable cells, from 416 original native WCVP modern trained climatic models.
methods.primary: Nonanalog climates censored, source-fixed bit masks.
methods.secondary: Extrapolation inclusion from original 0BP logistic reconstructed coefficients validated against unconsumed archived 21ka scores.
methods.sample_anchor_rule: MODERN sample localities are counterfactual geographic anchors, not ancient sites. A physically blocked cell is unavailable. Map passable anchors to the nearest potential host suitable cell within distance limit ONLY on the same 4-connected PMIP4 icefree landmass. Do not assign across disconnected ocean or ice.
methods.snap: Spherical unit vectors/KD tree; deterministic nearest by distance then grid index; no edge outcome used in matching.
methods.pair: Both localities assigned -> same or different predicted host-climate component; else exactly one/neither. Report conditional and unconditional denominators separately.
outputs: 513 per species, two time periods, primary vs extrapolation, 50/100/150 km distances
unique shared host-combination dependence; no claimed genetic effects
limits: Never equate modern anchor connectivity with realized 21ka plant occupancy or insect movement
No missing climate treated as unsuitable observation
Do not reopen negative TTF v0.5 known-host versus matched-other-plant comparison
No outcome-driven change of threshold/nearest radius/physical land criteria
